chunks: From him, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all together from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Al-Hakam, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who conditionally emancipates his slave, is there for him to retract with regards to it? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes. He is at the status of the bequest.

key_terms.يَرْجِعَ فِيهِ: To retract or revoke regarding it
key_terms.يُدَبِّرُ: To conditionally emancipate a slave upon death

ai.seo_question: Can a master revoke the conditional emancipation of his slave before death?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal status of the *Mudabbar* by equating the master's right to retract conditional emancipation with the revocation of a bequest (*wasiyyah*). This ruling highlights the fluidity of ownership rights during the master's lifetime, distinguishing the *Mudabbar* from a fully freed slave and establishing that the emancipation is not final until death occurs. The comparison to *wasiyyah* underscores that the act is a voluntary disposition of property that can be altered or revoked by the owner's will.

en.hubeali: From him, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazal Bin Shazan, both together from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who conditionally (upon his death) set free his slave, is there for him to retract with regards to it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes. He is at the status of the bequest’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from his father Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who makes his slave a Mudabbar; if he can change such decision. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, he can do so because it is like the will.’”
